fixes.explanation: Shepherd and King are good names, friend, but David doesn't use them in this line. He closes with "…O LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer." That comes right after he asks that the words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart be pleasing in God's sight. A shepherd needs a whole field of sheep, but a rock just sits there and holds, and I'm a stamper who knows how nice that sounds.

Light and Shield sound like a strong team, friend, like a buddy cop movie. But David doesn't use them here. He ends with "…O LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer." A rock is something you can stand on, and a redeemer is the One who buys you back. I know a little about being picked up for a quarter, so that last name hits me right in the handle.
